title: Sync pipeline state branch to remote for durability
summary: Architecture analysis for syncing the orchestrator's local-only `egg/pipeline-state` branch to remote and adding a schema compatibility layer for old pipeline state files. The recommended approach is push-at-phase-boundaries via the existing GatewayClient infrastructure, with fetch-on-startup for recovery. Schema drift is handled by a pre-validation sanitization function that normalizes unknown enum values and missing fields before Pydantic validation.

problem_statement.description: The orchestrator persists pipeline state on a local-only git branch (`egg/pipeline-state`) backed by a Docker named volume. This state is never synced to remote, meaning volume loss equals total state loss, cross-host recovery is impossible, and old pipelines cannot be inspected externally. Additionally, old pipeline state files with outdated schemas (e.g., removed `reviewer_unified` agent role) cause Pydantic ValidationError on every startup reconciliation indefinitely, with no migration path or cleanup mechanism.
goals: Push `egg/pipeline-state` branch to remote for durability against volume loss
Pull from remote on startup to restore state on fresh volumes or new hosts
Handle schema drift gracefully so old pipeline state files don't cause perpetual validation errors
Maintain the existing local-first performance characteristics — state saves must remain fast
Ensure push failures are non-blocking and don't disrupt pipeline execution

state_persistence.mechanism: Pipeline state is stored on a `egg/pipeline-state` orphan branch accessed via a persistent git worktree at `/home/egg/.egg-state/pipeline-worktree`. State files live at `.egg-state/pipelines/{id}.json`. Load uses `Pipeline.model_validate()`, save uses `model_dump_json()` + local git commit. Cross-process locking via `fcntl.flock` + in-process `threading.RLock`.
key_properties: Local-only: no `git push` ever happens for this branch (state_store.py:10)
Commits on every state change for issue-mode pipelines; phase-boundary-only for local-mode (state_store.py:477-480)
Lazy worktree creation with stale admin dir cleanup (state_store.py:188-235)

checkpoint_sync_pattern.mechanism: Checkpoints push to `egg/checkpoints/v2` using force-fetch + commit + push. Auth via GitHub token credential helper. Non-blocking — failures logged but never interrupt operations. Runs in daemon thread.
key_properties: Force-fetch with `+` prefix for conflict handling
Orphan branch created on first run
Multi-dimensional index maintained alongside data files
Runs in gateway process, not orchestrator

gateway_client_push_fetch.mechanism: GatewayClient provides `push_worktree_branch()` and `fetch_worktree_branch()` for best-effort remote syncing. Registers a temporary session, performs the operation via gateway API endpoints, then cleans up the session. Already used for worktree branch syncing at contract init, phase completion, and pipeline failure.
current_call_sites: After contract initialization — push statefiles so agents see them (routes/pipelines.py:4730-4736)
After phase completion — push statefiles before next phase (routes/pipelines.py:5501-5510)
On pipeline failure — backup work to remote (routes/pipelines.py:5396-5403)

startup_reconciliation.mechanism: On startup, iterates all pipelines with status=RUNNING and marks orphaned containers as FAILED. Calls `store.load_pipeline()` which can raise `StateValidationError` for old schemas. Current behavior: catch exception, log warning, skip pipeline — silently and repeatedly on every restart.
startup_reconciliation.validation_gap: When `load_pipeline()` encounters unknown enum values (e.g., `reviewer_unified` removed in commit e6706a916), `Pipeline.model_validate()` raises `ValidationError`, permanently making that pipeline inaccessible.

schema_compatibility.existing_pattern: DecisionStatus.TIMEOUT kept as vestigial enum value with comment 'kept for backwards compatibility with persisted pipeline state' (models.py:60). This is the only existing backwards-compat accommodation.
schema_compatibility.gap: AgentRole.REVIEWER_UNIFIED was removed with no such accommodation, breaking all old pipelines that used this role.

option_a_push_on_commit.description: After every `_commit_state()` call, push `egg/pipeline-state` to remote via the gateway. On startup, fetch from remote before creating the worktree.
pros: Full durability — every state change persisted remotely
Simple mental model — remote always has latest state
Proven pattern from checkpoint system
cons: High push frequency — pipeline state changes far more often than checkpoints
Every state save becomes a network round-trip through the gateway
Lock contention — flock would need to span the push operation
Push failures would either add latency (retry) or risk inconsistency (ignore)
option_a_push_on_commit.verdict: Rejected — latency and failure-mode complexity outweigh benefits for a state that changes dozens of times per phase

option_b_periodic_background_sync.description: Background thread pushes `egg/pipeline-state` to remote every 30-60 seconds. State saves remain local and fast.
pros: Decouples write latency from sync
Batches changes into single pushes
Failure-tolerant — retry on next cycle
cons: Bounded data loss window (up to one sync interval)
New component to maintain (periodic sync thread)
option_b_periodic_background_sync.verdict: Viable but over-engineered — introduces a new long-running component when phase-boundary pushes achieve nearly the same durability

option_c_push_at_phase_boundaries.description: Push to remote only at significant state transitions: pipeline creation, phase start, phase completion, and pipeline terminal states. Intermediate state changes remain local-only.
pros: Low push frequency — roughly 8-12 pushes per pipeline lifecycle
Captures the most important state transitions for recovery
Can be implemented by extending existing push_worktree_branch call sites
Intermediate agent status is already recoverable via startup reconciliation
No new components — integrates into existing phase transition code
cons: In-progress agent executions within a phase are not synced remotely
Must define which transitions trigger a push (adds a concept to reason about)
option_c_push_at_phase_boundaries.verdict: RECOMMENDED — best balance of durability, simplicity, and performance

option_i_pre_validation_sanitization.description: Before calling `Pipeline.model_validate(data)`, run a `sanitize_pipeline_data(data)` function that normalizes unknown enum values, adds missing fields with defaults, and removes unrecognized fields.
pros: Handles arbitrary schema drift — not tied to specific known changes
No changes to Pydantic models themselves
Can log what was sanitized for audit trail
Old state files become loadable without manual intervention
Straightforward to test in isolation
cons: Must track which fields contain enums and their valid values
Sanitized data may lose information (unknown values replaced)
Needs to be updated when new enum fields are added
option_i_pre_validation_sanitization.verdict: RECOMMENDED — broadest coverage with least model pollution

option_ii_model_validator.description: Add a `@model_validator(mode='before')` to Pipeline that normalizes known schema issues.
pros: Co-located with model — easy to find
Pydantic-native extension point
option_ii_model_validator.verdict: Viable but less clean — migration logic shouldn't live in the model

option_iii_versioned_migration_chain.description: Add `schema_version` field; on load, run migration chain (v1→v2, v2→v3, etc.) before validation.
pros: Clean separation
Standard pattern (Django, Alembic)
Explicit versioning
cons: Overkill for current frequency of schema changes
Existing state files have no version field
option_iii_versioned_migration_chain.verdict: Not recommended now — can be introduced later if schema changes become frequent

recommended_approach.remote_sync: Option C — Push at phase boundaries
recommended_approach.rationale: Phase-boundary pushing provides meaningful durability (volume loss only loses in-progress agent status within a phase, which is already recoverable via startup reconciliation) while keeping state saves fast and local. Pre-validation sanitization provides the broadest schema-drift coverage without polluting the Pydantic models.

changes.description: Add `push_state_branch()` method to StateStore that pushes the `egg/pipeline-state` branch to remote via a provided GatewayClient. The method performs a force-push of the state branch using a temporary session, mirroring the existing `push_worktree_branch()` pattern but targeting the state branch instead of a pipeline worktree branch. This is a best-effort operation — failures are logged but never block.
details: New method: `push_state_branch(self, gateway_client: GatewayClient) -> bool`
Uses gateway client to push the state branch (not the worktree branch)
Pushes from the state worktree directory
Returns True/False for success/failure, logs warnings on failure

changes.description: Add `fetch_state_branch()` method that fetches `egg/pipeline-state` from remote and resets the local worktree to match. Called on startup before serving requests. If the remote branch doesn't exist (first run), the method is a no-op. If the local branch has divergent commits, remote wins (the whole point is durability).
details: New method: `fetch_state_branch(self, gateway_client: GatewayClient) -> bool`
Fetches via gateway, then `git reset --hard origin/egg/pipeline-state` in the worktree
Returns True/False, logs warnings on failure
Gracefully handles: no remote branch, fetch failure, local-ahead divergence

changes.description: Add `push_state_branch()` and `fetch_state_branch()` convenience methods (or reuse existing push/fetch with appropriate parameters). The state worktree lives at a different path than pipeline worktrees, so the repo_path argument differs.
details: May reuse existing push_worktree_branch/fetch_worktree_branch with the state worktree path
Or add thin wrappers that set the correct refspec for the state branch

changes.description: On startup (cmd_serve), after startup reconciliation, call `state_store.fetch_state_branch()` to restore state from remote. This must happen before the health check framework initialization which iterates pipelines.
details: Insert fetch call between startup reconciliation and health check init
Best-effort — if fetch fails, continue with local state (backwards-compatible)

changes.description: Add `push_state_branch()` calls at phase boundaries. The existing code already pushes worktree branches at these points; add parallel state branch pushes.
details: After pipeline creation (create_pipeline route handler)
After phase start (within _start_pipeline_phase or equivalent)
After phase completion (existing push_worktree_branch call site at line ~5506)
After pipeline terminal state (COMPLETE, FAILED, CANCELLED)
All pushes are best-effort — wrapped in try/except with warning logging

key_decisions.decision: State branch push uses existing GatewayClient infrastructure
key_decisions.rationale: The orchestrator already has no direct GitHub token access. The gateway_client.py push/fetch methods provide authenticated git operations via temporary sessions. Reusing this avoids introducing a new auth pathway.
alternatives_rejected: Direct git push from orchestrator (no token access)
New gateway endpoint specific to state branch (unnecessary — generic push works)

key_decisions.decision: Remote wins on startup fetch (overwrite local)
key_decisions.rationale: The purpose of remote sync is durability. If local state is stale (volume loss, new host), remote is the source of truth. If local has unpushed changes (unlikely edge case — means last push failed), they represent at most one phase boundary of drift.
alternatives_rejected: Merge (complex, error-prone for JSON state files)

key_decisions.decision: Push at phase boundaries, not on every commit
key_decisions.rationale: Pipeline state changes dozens of times per phase (agent heartbeats, container status updates). Phase boundaries (8-12 per lifecycle) capture the recovery-relevant transitions. Intermediate state is already recoverable via startup reconciliation.
alternatives_rejected: Push on every commit (too frequent, adds latency)

work_area_2_schema_sanitization.title: Pre-validation sanitization for old pipeline state files

changes.description: Add `sanitize_pipeline_data(data: dict) -> dict` function that normalizes pipeline state data before Pydantic validation. This function walks the nested structure and replaces unknown enum values with sensible defaults or drops the containing objects.
details: Build sets of valid enum values from the model enums at module level
For AgentRole: if unknown, drop the AgentExecution from the agents list (with log warning)
For PipelineStatus, PipelinePhase, etc.: if unknown, map to a safe default (e.g., FAILED for status)
For ContainerStatus, AgentExecutionStatus: if unknown, map to FAILED
For DecisionStatus: if unknown, map to CANCELLED
Handle missing fields by letting Pydantic defaults fill them (no action needed)
Handle extra/unrecognized top-level fields by removing them (Pydantic strict mode)
Return the sanitized dict — caller passes it to Pipeline.model_validate()

changes.description: Modify `load_pipeline()` to call `sanitize_pipeline_data()` before `Pipeline.model_validate()`. If sanitization changes anything, optionally re-save the sanitized version (auto-migration).
details: Replace: `Pipeline.model_validate(data)` with: `sanitized = sanitize_pipeline_data(data); Pipeline.model_validate(sanitized)`
Log at INFO level what was sanitized (e.g., 'Sanitized pipeline issue-500: dropped 2 agents with unknown role reviewer_unified')
Optionally: if data != sanitized, re-save to migrate the file on disk (auto-heal)

key_decisions.decision: Drop agents with unknown roles rather than mapping to a replacement
key_decisions.rationale: Unknown roles represent agents from a different schema era. Mapping `reviewer_unified` to `reviewer_code` would misrepresent historical data. Since these pipelines are terminal (old, completed/failed), accurate representation matters less than loadability. Dropping the unrecognized agent preserves the rest of the pipeline state.

key_decisions.decision: Sanitize before validation, not inside the model
key_decisions.rationale: Keeps migration logic separate from the data model. The model validates the present; the sanitizer handles the past. This is easier to test and doesn't accumulate debt in the model definition.
alternatives_rejected: Versioned migration chain (overkill for current frequency)

dependencies_and_constraints.gateway_dependency: All remote push/fetch operations go through the gateway sidecar. The gateway must be healthy for sync to work. This is already the case for worktree branch pushes — the same failure mode applies.
dependencies_and_constraints.branch_ownership: The `egg/pipeline-state` branch already follows the `egg/` prefix convention required by the gateway's branch ownership policy.
dependencies_and_constraints.single_writer: The orchestrator is currently single-instance. If multi-orchestrator support is added in the future, the push-at-phase-boundary approach would need conflict handling (force-push or last-writer-wins). This is explicitly out of scope for this issue.
dependencies_and_constraints.backwards_compatible_startup: The fetch-on-startup behavior must be backwards-compatible: if the remote branch doesn't exist (pre-feature orchestrator or first run), startup proceeds normally with local-only state.
dependencies_and_constraints.no_new_dependencies: The implementation uses only existing infrastructure (GatewayClient, state_store git operations). No new Python packages or gateway endpoints are needed.

risks.risk: Push failure during phase boundary leaves remote state stale
risks.mitigation: Pushes are best-effort and non-blocking, same as existing worktree branch pushes. Subsequent phase boundary pushes will catch up. The window of data loss is bounded to one phase.

risks.risk: Startup fetch from remote overwrites local state that hasn't been pushed
risks.mitigation: This only happens if the last push failed AND the volume was lost — a double-failure scenario. In this case, remote state is still more recent than empty state. If the volume is intact, local state is more recent and the fetch is effectively a no-op (local is ahead).

risks.risk: Sanitization drops data from old pipelines that users want to inspect
risks.mitigation: Sanitization only drops individual agent executions with unknown roles, not entire pipelines. The pipeline itself and all recognizable data is preserved. Original JSON files are available in git history.

risks.risk: Force-push of state branch could conflict with concurrent pushes
risks.mitigation: Single-orchestrator architecture makes this a non-issue. Documented as a constraint for future multi-orchestrator support.

open_questions_resolved.question: Push frequency threshold — should pipeline creation and terminal states also trigger pushes?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Yes. Push at: pipeline creation, phase start, phase completion, pipeline terminal states (COMPLETE, FAILED, CANCELLED). This gives roughly 10-14 pushes per pipeline lifecycle.

open_questions_resolved.question: Startup fetch behavior when remote is newer than local?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Remote wins. `git fetch` + `git reset --hard origin/egg/pipeline-state`. If local has unpushed changes, they are overwritten — this represents at most one phase boundary of drift.

open_questions_resolved.question: Startup fetch failure handling?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Proceed with local state (option c from the analysis). Best-effort fetch. This is backwards-compatible — pre-feature orchestrators had no remote state and worked fine.

open_questions_resolved.question: Old pipeline cleanup?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Out of scope for this issue. Cleanup/archival is a separate concern that can be addressed independently.

open_questions_resolved.question: Unknown enum handling strategy?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Drop the containing object (e.g., remove agent execution with unknown role). Log a warning with the pipeline ID and dropped value. This preserves the pipeline while discarding unrecognizable sub-objects.

open_questions_resolved.question: Gateway push API — new endpoint or reuse existing?
open_questions_resolved.resolution: Reuse existing GatewayClient.push_worktree_branch() and fetch_worktree_branch() with the state worktree path and state branch refspec. No new gateway endpoints needed.
